main_text.p: ἐχτὰ μεταφορᾶν, alias quidem robur exercituum, & succisionis Libani φράσσω, internecionem exercitus significari. Vt Isa.10. 13. Ecce Dominator Iehouah exercituum excidet ramū cū robore, & excelsi statura succisi, & sublimes humiliabūtur. 34. Succidetq; arbores perplexas sylvæ ferro, & Lybanus ferro forti cadet. Alias uero significat uberrimas & florentisimas prouincias. Nahum.1.4. Qui increpat mare, & exiccat illud, omnia quoq; flumina siccare solet: desolatus est Basan & Charmel, & flos Libani desolatus est.
main_text.head: DE LIBANO MONTE, ET sylua Cedrina.
main_text.p: Strabo lib.16. Geograph. Duo montes sunt qui Cœlesyriam includunt, æqualibus fere inter se difsiti spacijs, Libanus & Antilibanus, paulò supra mare incipientes: Libanus prope Tripolin & Dei facie: Antilibanus supra mare Sidoniū. definunt autem ad Arabiæ montes, qui sunt ultra Damascum, & eos qui ibi Trachonitæ dicuntur, qui glebosos atq; fructiferos colles habent, &c.
Ptolemæus Geographiæ lib 5. cap.15. in descriptione Syriæ & eius montium, s 2 memia

page.notes: The Greek words in the first line are only approximately rendered (ἐχτὰ / μεταφορᾶν and φράσσω) and are uncertain. "succisionis" and "succisi" are read from the scan and may be unclear. The signature "s 2" at the foot is partly obscured; the catchword "memia" is partly damaged and read as "memi·" with a possible [?].
